questions.question: If 13 December 1969 is Saturday, then what will be the day of the week on 9 July 1978?
questions.solution:
Given : 13 December 1969 was Saturday

Explanation :

The number of odd days from 13 December 1969 to 9 July 1978 :

 
 

 Year
 Period
 Calculation
 Odd days
 
 

 1969
 13 December 1969 - 31 December 1969
 18 days
 18 ÷ 7 = 4
 
 

 1970 - 2077
 Full years (6 Ordinary years + 2 Leap years)
 (1 odd day × 6 Ordinary years) + (2 odd days × 2 Leap years) = 10 odd days
 10 ÷ 7 = 3
 
 

 1978
 1st January 1978 - 9 July 1978
 31 January + 28 February + 31 March + 30 April + 31 May + 30 June + 9 July = 190 days 
 190 ÷ 7 = 1
 
 

 Total odd days
 (8 ÷ 7) = **1**
 
 

∴ The number of odd days from 13 December 1969 to 9 July 1978 ⇒ 1

⇒So, One odd day get added to Saturday because day asked in future.

∴ Sunday was the day of the week on the 9 July 1978.

Hence, "**Sunday**" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements :**

All blue are dogs.

No dog is silver

All pink are dogs.

**Conclusions : **

(I) Some pink are silver.

(II) No blue is pink is a possibility.

(III) Some blue are silver

options.text: Both conclusions II and III follow
Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc61d416a5142f2e1714a356015da5951345bfd3660949c149fe27ff6dad4742.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some pink are silver → **Does not** Follow (As, all pink are dogs and no dog is silver, So, no pink will be silver, therefore Some pink are silver will be definitely false)

II. No blue is pink is a possibility → Follow (As, all blue are dogs and all pink are dogs. and, no definite relation is given between blue and pink, so No blue is pink can be possible therefore it is definitely true)

III. Some blue are silver → Does not Follow (As, all blue are dogs and no dog is silver. So, no blue will be silver, therefore Some blue are silver is definitely false)

Here, Only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Only conclusion II follows**".

So,
